correctness.rationale: P29 is explicitly the degree-14 quadratic-residue graph over F29, and N is open (not closed) neighborhood complex. Independent code constructed all 449,153 faces by 29 neighborhood downsets; checked the exact f-vector. Natural-order matching gave 224,409 pairs, critical cells one 0-cell, 138 3-cells and 195 4-cells and topological acyclicity of all 3,225,264 Hasse arrows. Exact signed 138x195 Morse differential has 3,843 nonzero entries: 117 unimodular pivots and 21x78 residual with 21x14 Hermite basis of 14 unit Smith invariants, total rank131 with only unit elementary divisors. A different even/odd vertex order produced 117 3-cells and 174 4-cells and again ranks 7,64 with unit Smith factors. Because pi3 of the 3-skeleton bouquet is free generated by degree maps and the image is primitive, CW cancellation gives wedge7 S3 vee wedge64 S4, not only integral homology. Multiplication by 2 is a nonresidue complement isomorphism, and the published N(complement G) Alexander-dual identity gives dominance H22=Z64 H23=Z7 by the integer universal coefficients. No homotopy type for dominance claimed.

value.rationale: The Paley graph of order 29 is a canonical self-complementary strongly regular/quadratic-residue graph; its open-neighborhood complex is a natural topological invariant relevant to chromatic graph topology. Exact integral torsion-freeness and a mixed-dimensional sphere-wedge stand in sharp mathematical contrast to Paley17 open-neighborhood three-torsion and Paley29 independence/Rips complexes, answering an independent natural exact-invariant question. Dominance homology is a useful formal consequence of known duality, not counted as independently novel.
